newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stora says weak demand behind 9-mo slump.
newsitem.headline: Stora says weak demand behind 9-mo slump.

text.p: Swedish forestry group Stora posted on Thursday a sharp drop in profits for the first nine months of the year, saying pulp operations had been hit by slack demand and weak prices.
Stora's profit after financial items plummeted to 1.92 billion from 6.19 billion crowns compared to the corresponding 1995 period, while sales slumped to 34.25 billion crowns from 43.26 billion.
The result was in line with expectations. A Reuters poll found analysts expected a profit after financial items of 1.89 billion crowns.
"The change is attributable to delivery volumes declining by eight percent, coupled with a deterioration in prices for virtually all products," Stora said in a statement.
"In addition, the strengthened crown had an adverse effect on invoicing in an amount of 2.5 billion crowns."
It said the divestment of the units Stora Building Products and Newton Falls accounted for a further 1.8 billion crowns of the downturn in sales.
Operating income slumped to 2.32 billion crowns from 6.98 billion a year earlier.
"Income was adversely affected by lower prices and delivery volumes totalling 3.3 billion crowns, as well as by 625 million crowns due to the appreciation of the crown," Stora said.
"The remainder of the decline was attributable to changeovers and start-ups in connection with plant inventories, lower revenues of a non-recurring nature and the revaluation of inventories."
Stora said a weak economic trend in Europe affected markets for paper and board.
Demand in the U.S. was slightly better due to a stronger economic trend but deliveries were lower than a year ago.

Order bookings for pulp, paper and board improved in the second quarter but were calm in the third quarter for seasonal reasons and due to lower shipments to Southeast Asia after the high levels recording during the early summer.
Demand for fine papers remained stable.
The order situation also improved in the board and packaging paper area, particularly for liner and fluting.
Towards the end of the third quarter order bookings for uncoated (SC) and coated (LWC) magazine papers, in the printing papers product area, strengthened.
Prices for pulp, LWC, fine papers and board fell in the first half of the year due to the weak market.
However prices for paper pulp increased in the third quarter. Fine paper prices were raised in September by about 10 percent in all European markets.
Stora said the brakes had now been applied to the price decline for board.
"Translated into Swedish crowns, average prices for Stora's pulp, paper and board products were 16 percent lower, compared with the corresponding period of 1995," Stora said.
Total deliveries slipped eight percent.
"Stora estimates the underlying consumption of paper and board has continued to rise and that the decrease in deliveries is due to inventory adjustments," the company said.
Earnings in most areas declined, including pulp.
